Mr. Kamal Hossain, Advocate, For the petitioners 
Mr. Md. Mizanur Rahman, Advocate, For the opposite parties.
parties:
Rezia Bewa and others
Vs.
Md. Tamizuddin and others.
full_judgment:
2. The facts giving rise to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite parties No.01-145 as plaintiffs instituted the original Other Class Suit No.26 of 1999 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Kalihati, Tangail for declaration of their easement right to the suit pond described in the schedule of the plaint contending inter alia that the suit pond appertaining to settlement khatian No.39 comprising an area of 1.07 acres of land in plot No.181 under Mouza Nigoir of Kalihati police station of District-Tangail originally belonged to landlord Sreenath Bhattacharjee. One Biswanath Bhattacharjee under the landlord Sreenath Bhattacharjee being an authorized person prepared the suit pond useable for the inhabitants of the locality and thereafter surrendered in favour of the villagers of the concerned village which is commonly known as 'Bara Pukur'. The inhabitants of the locality since the regime of Ex-landlord, using the suit pond Tara Pukur' for their necessity and subsequently for the interest of the villagers, they prepared a Mosjid and Madrasha namely "Forkania Ebtedaye Madrasha" in the bank of the pond for their own use and accordingly the villagers use to possess the water of the pond and also using the holy Mosjid and Madrasha. The further case of the plaintiff No.01, Md. Tomijuddin and 149 persons, who on behalf of all the villagers of the concerned locality instituted the suit in representative character under the provisions laid down in Order I, rule 8 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the predecessor of the present petitioners namely Abdul Rashid Miah out of ill-motive to grab the suit pond managed to create a false pattannama which is a: forged and anti-dated paper and in collusion with the concerned officials the predecessor of the present petitioners managed to create a collusive R.S. khatian being No.44 in his name. it is also the case of the plaintiffs that, despite; the predecessor of the defendants created the false papers showing his tenancy right, he never possessed the suit pond and after his demise the legal heirs of Abdul Rashid, who are the present defendant-petitioners also do not possess the suit pond. The matter of preparation of R.S. record in the name of Abdur Rashid was suppressed by the defendants all along and for the first time in the 1st part of Chaitra, 1405 B.S. they disclosing about the R.S. record in the name of their predecessor declared that they will possess the suit pond and on hearing that, the people of the locality being aggrieved instituted the original suit. 

 3. The contrary case of the defendant-petitioners in short is thus that Abdur Rashid, the predecessor of the present defendant-petitioners obtained the suit property by way of a pattan from the ex-Zamindar Biswanath Bhattacharjee in the year 1345 B.S. and after taking pattan, Abdur Rashid paid rents and obtained `Dakhilas'. Subsequently, during S.A. operation the property has been correctly recorded in the name of Abdur Rashid in Khatian No.44. The further case of the defendants is such that Abdur Rashid while owning and possessing the suit property, by a registered Heba dated 08.12.1990 gifted the suit property in favour of the defendant No.4, who is the contesting defendant to the original suit. Possession was delivered in favour of the defendant No.4 and the defendant after re-excavating the suit pond within the knowledge of all, using the property-in- dispute peacefully, but the plaintiffs out of ill-motive to grab the property on false allegations filed the suit which is vexatious and false. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule controverted the argument advanced from the side of the petitioners and submits that the learned Appellate Court during disposal of the appeal committed no illegality, infirmity or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned court of appeal below at the time of deciding the merit of the appeal, properly complied with the provisions laid down in Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and on due assessment of evidence in its true perspective arrived at a conclusive decision that the suit is maintainable as framed and the plaintiffs as representatives of the inhabitants of the localities concern, successfully discharged their onus of proof by adducing sufficient credible, tangible evidence. The learned Advocate submits that in fact, the plaintiffs instituted the original suit for easement right lawfully against the servient owners of the suit pond, inasmuch as; the legal heirs of the Ex-Chairman of the concerned Union Parishad, Abdur Rashid on the basis of their fictitious claim denied the easement right of the villagers to the suit pond, and since the S.A. record of right has been prepared in the name of Abdur Rashid, the original suit has been instituted against the legal heirs of Abdur Rashid Miah, and from the very facts of the suit it is clear that the defendants are the servient owners of the suit pond in absence of Abdur Rashid and the original owner Ex-Zamindar. Therefore, there exist no legal embargo in filing the suit for easement right as instituted. The learned Advocate also submits that the witnesses adduced from the side of the defendants, in their testimonies disproved their own case of acquisition of title and possession in the suit pond on the basis of pattan from Ex-Zamindar and on the contrary, they have proved the case of the plaintiffs in their testimonies and the matter has been properly addressed by the learned appellate court in the impugned judgment and decree. The learned Advocate lastly submits that, admittedly the defendants are the legal heirs of Abdur Rashid Mia, who is the S.A. recorded tenant and the S.A. khatian No.45 stands recorded in the name of Abdur Rasid Mia. From the testimony of the plaintiff's witnesses and from the pleading's case of the plaintiffs it is apparent that neither Abdur Rashid during his life time, nor after his death the heirs of Abdur Rashid ever tried to dispossess the plaintiffs and as such under section 33 and 35 of the Easement Act, there lies no scope to file any suit for injunction and as because the plaintiff's right to easement right has been denied from the side of the defendants, the plaintiffs lawfully instituted the original suit under the above provisions of law. In the concluding submission, the learned Advocate argued that in the impugned judgment and decree there is no misreading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. 

 10. In order to appreciate the argument advanced from the sides of the learned counsels for the respective parties, having gone through the pleadings of the parties, the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial Court dated 27.06.2000 in Other Class Suit No.26 of 1999, the impugned judgment and decree dated 24.04.2003 passed by the learned appellate court, the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties along with the case records, it transpires that admittedly the suit property appertaining to Mouza Negoir under Kalihati police station of District-Tangail is a big pond which is commonly known as Tara Pukur', and that has been recorded in settlement khatian No.39 in the name of landlord Sreenath Bhattacharjee. Under the landlord the authorized person of the suit pond was one Biswanath Bhattacharjee, son of Loknath Bhattacharjee. It is the specific contention of the plaintiffs, who are the representatives of four neighboring villages namely `Negoir', `Manduria', `Vukta' and `Akua' that they have instituted the original suit for a declaration of their easement right after compliance of the provisions laid down in Order I rule 8 of the Code of Civil Procedure and on perusal of the original case record it is evident that the mandatory requirement of law with regard to publication of notice has been complied with by the plaintiffs. It has been asserted by the plaintiffs in their pleadings that the authorized person of the suit pond under the Zamindar Sreenath Bhattacharjee surrendered possession of the suit pond in favour of the villagers of village Negoir, Monduria, Vukta and Akua, which are adjacent to one another, to meet up their basic need of water. The suit pond under admitted settlement plot No.181 consists an area of 1.07 acres and it is the case of the plaintiffs that the villagers of the concerned locality from the regime of Ex. Zaminders, using the water of the suit pond and for their basic necessity they have erected a Mosque and a Madrasha in the bank of the pond Tara Pukur'. The holy mosque and the madrasha namely Torkania Ebtedaye Madras ha' are being managed by selling the fishes of the suit pond Tara pukur'. It is also the case of the plaintiffs in their pleadings that, beside the Madrasha there exist a graveyard of the villagers and the predecessor of the present defendant-petitioners Abdur Rashid Mia collusively to grab the suit pond in the name of pattan, created a forged pattannama and subsequently he also managed the settlement officials and during S.A. operation he has prepared the S.A. record in his name illegally using his power of Union Parishad Chairman showing his right, title, interest in the suit pond. 

 12. To substantiate the respective cases of the parties, the parties to the suit have adduced evidence and from the side of the plaintiffs they have examined as many as 08(eight) witnesses and on the other hand, the defendants have examined 05(five) witnesses. They also submitted some documentary evidence marked as Exhibit-`Ka', `Kha' series, `Ga' and their basic document pattannama in the name of Abdur Rashid Mia has been marked as Exhibit-`Gha'. The Hebanama deed dated 08.12.1990 in the name of defendant No.04 executed by Abdur Rashid is Exhibit-`Ga'. Exhibit-`Ka' is the relevant S.A. khatian of which stands recorded in the name of defendant-petitioner's predecessor, Abdur Rashid Mia. The other papers Exhibit-`Kha' series are the government rent receipts by which the defendants paid rents by virtue of their predecessor's record of right. 

 21. On the contrary, the defendant's witness D.W.1 Golam Mostafa @ Tula Munshi, who is the defendant No.4 testified that the suit property was the 'Mash' land under Elenga Zamindar and previously it was a pond and subsequently it has been pattan settled and has become a cultivable land and his father Abdur Rashid in the year 1345 B.S. took pattan of the said land from the Zamindar and did Toro' cultivation there. D.W.1 further testified that his father Abdur Rashid in the year 1990 made a registered Heba deed in his (D.W.1) favour and after getting the land, this witness re-excavated the pond in the suit land and using the same. During cross-examination the defendant No.4 testified at a stage that he does not know as to whether the S.A. khatian was prepared by the concerned officials, sitting in their (defendants) homestead. With regard to pattan of his father in a reply to a question, D.W.1 testified that he cannot understand the writings of pattan, but in the pattan there is a recital 'Pukur' and in plot No.181 the area of land is 1.07 acres and the pattannama was not written in front of him (D.W. 1) and he does not know as to whether any registered ‘kabuliyate' is required for getting pattan, but he knows that for getting pattan, rent is to be paid at the time of granting pattan. During cross-examination D.W.1 further testified at a stage in a reply to a question from the side of the plaintiffs that, in the suit pond there are fishes. This witness (defendant No. 4) admitted in his cross-examination that in the bank of the suit pond there is a 'Mosque' and a `Madrasha'. This witness in his cross-examination categorically testified that the mosque is running at the expenditure of local people and he cannot say, who is the Secretary of that Mosque.
